name: PA-15
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Glenn Thompson seeking re-election with large financial edge
No polls or expert ratings; markets price Thompson at 96%
Democratic challenger outraised roughly ten to one
model.rationale: The R+19 district lean, Thompson's incumbency and his roughly tenfold fundraising advantage over Ray Bilger all point to a comfortable Republican hold, and prediction markets price his win at 96%. With no polls or expert ratings to the contrary, the forecast stays near the fundamentals.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the incumbent under 60% or a surge of Democratic outside spending would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Glenn Thompson, the Republican incumbent, is seeking another term in a north-central Pennsylvania district that leans about 19 points Republican. He has raised about $2.1 million and holds a large cash advantage over Democrat Ray Bilger, who has raised roughly $210,000 with little outside help. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Thompson about a 96% chance of winning.

The forecast rests on the district's strong partisan lean, Thompson's incumbency, and his financial edge, pointing to a comfortable Republican win of roughly 18 points. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling, so the error band is somewhat wide, but there is little evidence suggesting the race is competitive.
